gen_risks.description: Ongoing conflict in South Sudan could worsen regional instability, driving further refugee influxes into Uganda and overstretching local public services and water natural resources.
gen_risks.mitigation: Coordinate closely with UNHCR and OPM through the Comprehensive Refugee Response Framework (CRRF) and invest in long-term sustainable water supply infrastructure in hosting districts.
gen_risks.evidence: The most critical risk to this outlook is regional instability, particularly from the ongoing conflict in South Sudan.

gen_risks.description: Fiduciary and contract management weaknesses within MWE and NWSC could cause processing delays, multiple contract amendments, and significant time/cost overruns during civil works execution.
gen_risks.mitigation: Recruit dedicated procurement consultants, conduct capacity-building training on World Bank Procurement Regulations, and implement contract management plans for high-value contracts.
gen_risks.evidence: weakness resulted in multiple amendments during contract implementation resulting in cost and time overruns.

gen_risks.description: Incomplete needs assessments and inadequate geotechnical studies prior to construction could lead to extensive design changes and variations during contract implementation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Require outcome-based needs assessments and comprehensive geotechnical studies during the detailed engineering design phase prior to bidding.
gen_risks.evidence: incomplete needs assessments and inadequate attention to geotechnical studies leading to design changes/variations during implementation

gen_risks.description: Limited capacity of local domestic contractors to execute complex water and sanitation projects could result in slow construction progress or sub-standard work quality.
gen_risks.mitigation: Package works contracts to match market capacity, encourage joint ventures and subconsultants, and utilize open international competitive procurement.
gen_risks.evidence: limited capacity of domestic contractors to conduct projects of this nature, complexity, and scope

gen_risks.description: Incomplete operationalization of the project module within MWE's Integrated Financial Management System (IFMS) increases the risk of financial reporting errors and processing delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Fully operationalize the IFMS project module at MWE and maintain qualified financial management specialists within the Project Support Team.
gen_risks.evidence: the project module of the IFMS has not been fully operationalized at the MWE, which increases the risk of errors

gen_risks.description: High climate variability, extreme temperatures, and intense rainfall events could cause severe water stress, flooding, and physical damage to raw water intakes and infrastructure.
gen_risks.mitigation: Integrate climate-resilient engineering designs, implement water source buffer protection, and conduct catchment management activities such as reforestation and soil conservation.
gen_risks.evidence: high climate variability and underdeveloped water resources infrastructure could result in significant water stress in areas of the country.

gen_risks.description: An influx of construction labor into project host communities could trigger social conflicts, gender-based violence (GBV), sexual exploitation, and increased local transmission of STDs/HIV.
gen_risks.mitigation: Mandate worker codes of conduct, enforce labor influx management plans, maximize local workforce recruitment, and conduct mandatory GBV and HIV prevention training.
gen_risks.evidence: Long walks to water sources trigger serious social consequences, particularly GBV... Labor influx... potential GBV in Project areas.

gen_risks.description: Land acquisition and pipeline rights-of-way alignment could cause physical and temporary economic displacement of local populations, leading to grievances and land disputes.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop and implement site-specific Resettlement Action Plans (RAPs) prior to civil works, pay timely compensation, and establish functional local Grievance Redress Mechanisms.
gen_risks.evidence: road encroachment and potential works like plants, pump stations and storage tanks may have land acquisition implications and displacement

gen_risks.description: Insufficient dry-season river flows in the Namatala River could undermine water supply reliability for Mbale Town while breaching required downstream environmental flow thresholds.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct an Augmented Water Supply Study before construction to evaluate source impoundment, borehole supplementation, and alternative supply expansion options.
gen_risks.evidence: Namatala’s dry weather flows in some cases may not be sufficient to meet projected water demand and maintain an adequate EF.

gen_risks.description: Regional Umbrella Water Authorities (UWAs) may experience initial operating losses in newly gazetted small towns due to low revenue collection rates and high initial operation costs.
gen_risks.mitigation: Enforce cost-reflective tariffs with a minimum 25% margin, automate tariff adjustments, convert systems to low-cost solar power, and apply performance-based operator contracts.
gen_risks.evidence: Several of the systems will show operating losses in the first years of operation, but these losses will gradually decrease

gen_risks.description: Improper operation of fecal sludge treatment facilities and wastewater lagoons could cause untreated effluent discharges, odor nuisance, water body contamination, and public health risks.
gen_risks.mitigation: Ensure facility designs include percolate treatment, construct watertight structures, provide operator training, and regularly monitor treated effluent quality against NEMA standards.
gen_risks.evidence: sludge management and wastewater effluent discharges that exceed standards; possible impacts on surface and/or ground water due to leakages

gen_risks.description: Lack of structured coordination among humanitarian partners, local governments, and MWE in refugee districts could result in ill-sited boreholes and groundwater contamination risks.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish formal multi-agency coordination mechanisms under MWE, OPM, and UNHCR to streamline water resource planning and borehole positioning.
gen_risks.evidence: lack of coordination resulted in boreholes being drilled too close to each other or too close to shallow pit latrines, risking contamination

gen_risks.description: Prolonged internal administrative approval processes within government agencies could delay payments to vendors and contractors, slowing project execution.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish an automated payment tracking system, enforce payment processing timelines, and strengthen internal audit and accounting workflows.
gen_risks.evidence: delays in paying vendors due to prolonged internal approval processes.

gen_risks.description: Shifting refugee settlements from free emergency humanitarian water supply to paid user-tariff schemes under public utilities may meet social resistance or policy transition hurdles.
gen_risks.mitigation: Collaborate with UNHCR and OPM on designing progressive refugee tariff policies linked to socio-economic support and conduct extensive community consultation.
gen_risks.evidence: refugees in settlements currently do not pay for water, the UNHCR and OPM are collaborating with the MWE on designing a new water tariff policy

gen_risks.description: Over-reliance on diesel-powered mechanized pumping schemes exposes water schemes to high fuel costs, volatile operational expenses, and frequent service interruptions.
gen_risks.mitigation: Prioritize solar-powered piped water systems and gravity-fed schemes during project design to minimize diesel reliance and lower running costs.
gen_risks.evidence: long-term savings on fuel and capital maintenance make solar pumping systems more cost-effective than alternative mechanized pumping systems.

gen_risks.description: Turnover of qualified financial management and procurement staff within MWE and NWSC could impair institutional memory and slow project implementation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Maintain competitive staffing conditions, recruit dedicated PST specialists, and conduct regular hand-holding training sessions.
gen_risks.evidence: turnover of qualified and experienced staff is noticed.

gt_risks.description: Political and governance risk: as detailed in the CPF, significant political uncertainty is not foreseen, but governance and effective public-sector management present substantial risks.
gt_risks.mitigation: The Project will mitigate these risks through (a) strengthening the MWE's regulatory framework; (b) carrying out a citizen engagement strategy; and (c) strengthening project implementation efforts in close coordination with local government officials and development partners. The World Bank's procurement processes will also help safeguard the Project from corruption.

gt_risks.description: Institutional capacity for implementation and sustainability risk: the Umbrella Water Authority (UWA) as a regional service delivery model for small towns and RGCs was recently introduced. Although the decision to scale up this model was informed by extensive analytical work and a pilot project, the UWA model was only recently operationalized.
gt_risks.mitigation: The Project will support implementation of a professionalized monitoring system focused on enhancing revenue collection approaches (billing software, cashless/mobile payment systems) and on strengthening integration of specialized private operators through improved contract management. The implementation team will use the Utility Performance Monitoring and Information System (UPMIS) tool to regularly review UWA and NWSC performance.

gt_risks.description: Fiduciary risk: the Procurement risk is rated Substantial while the FM risk is Moderate. The risks identified relate to delays and skills gaps at different stages of procurement processing.
gt_risks.mitigation: IWMDP will benefit from the lessons learned and mechanisms put in place under the predecessor project (WMDP); detailed mitigation measures for the procurement risk are set out in the Appraisal (Procurement) section.

gt_risks.description: The environmental and social risk is deemed Substantial given (a) potential opposition to the introduction of a new service delivery model, including new tariffs and catchment management measures; (b) the influx of new workers in small towns and RGCs; and (c) potentially adverse environmental impacts from the construction and operation of the proposed investments.
gt_risks.mitigation: The environmental and social risk will be managed through the application of an Environmental and Social Management Framework (ESMF), a Resettlement Policy Framework (RPF), and related safeguards instruments (Environmental and Social Impact Assessment, Resettlement Action Plans).

gt_risks.description: Other risks (social tensions in districts hosting refugees): tensions between refugees and citizens are caused by inequity in access to and payment for water supply and sanitation (WSS) services. While refugees in the settlements benefit from humanitarian aid and GoU support, Ugandans in host communities receive limited support for services and infrastructure, causing social tension that may result in Project implementation delays given potential community opposition to the works.
gt_risks.mitigation: The GoU has prioritized development efforts for poor districts hosting refugees while remaining firmly committed to its policy on refugee protection. The Project will manage this risk by designing WSS facilities and catchment management measures that benefit both host communities and refugees, and by ensuring the Project's social and communication management plan is applied and adequately supervised. There are no known existing risks to the refugee protection framework or reputational risks for the Project.
